description: Check whether the Expedia API is available.
Find cities, neighbourhoods, landmarks, airports and hotels by name  -  mints the region_id, hotel_id and airport_code every search takes.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
**What the traveller typed  -  the start of a city, neighbourhood, landmark, airport or hotel name** (e.g. `new york`, `times sq`, `JFK`, `hilton paris`). Required, 1 - 100 characters.

Results come back as you would see them in a search box, best match first. A US ZIP code (e.g. `10001`, on the `us` market) answers with an `ADDRESS` suggestion. Plain text only: angle brackets, braces, backslashes, back-ticks, `..` and comment markers are rejected with a 400 (the storefront blocks such text as an attack).

schema.description:

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
**Which kind of trip the suggestions are for**  -  it changes which places are suggested and in what order. Optional; defaults to `hotels`.

- `hotels`  -  cities, neighbourhoods, landmarks, airports and individual hotels (use for every /hotels/* endpoint)
- `flights`  -  airports and metro-area codes first
- `cars`  -  car pick-up points: airports, city areas and hotels
- `activities`  -  wider "and vicinity" regions, cities and landmarks
- `packages`  -  metro-area codes, airports and cities

description: Search hotels in a destination with dates, guests, sort and filters.

parameters.name: region_id
parameters.description:
**Where to search, as a `region_id` from `/locations`**  -  a city, neighbourhood, landmark, airport or wider region (e.g. `178293` for New York and vicinity, `2734` for Paris). Send this or `destination`.

The most reliable way to name a destination: the id means the same place on every market. An id that matches no destination returns a 404.

schema.description:
**Where to search, as a `region_id` from `/locations`**  -  a city, neighbourhood, landmark, airport or wider region (e.g. `178293` for New York and vicinity, `2734` for Paris). Send this or `destination`.

The most reliable way to name a destination: the id means the same place on every market. An id that matches no destination returns a 404.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description:
**Where to search, as free text** (e.g. `Paris, France`, `Lake Tahoe`, `Las Vegas`). Used only when `region_id` is not sent.

The text is matched to the closest known destination and the matched place is echoed as `destination.resolved_region_id` and `destination.resolved_name`  -  check them, because the matching is loose and a vague or misspelt name can match somewhere unexpected (`blorfington` → "Mall of America, Bloomington, Minnesota"). Text that matches nothing returns a 404. For precise control use `/locations` and pass `region_id`.

schema.description:
**Where to search, as free text** (e.g. `Paris, France`, `Lake Tahoe`, `Las Vegas`). Used only when `region_id` is not sent.

The text is matched to the closest known destination and the matched place is echoed as `destination.resolved_region_id` and `destination.resolved_name`  -  check them, because the matching is loose and a vague or misspelt name can match somewhere unexpected (`blorfington` → "Mall of America, Bloomington, Minnesota"). Text that matches nothing returns a 404. For precise control use `/locations` and pass `region_id`.

parameters.name: check_in
parameters.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-05`). Send it together with `check_out`; the two are validated as a pair.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. When both dates are omitted, prices are quoted for a one-night stay the storefront chooses (about two weeks out) and that stay is reported under `priced_for` in the response  -  send your own dates for prices you can rely on.

schema.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-05`). Send it together with `check_out`; the two are validated as a pair.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. When both dates are omitted, prices are quoted for a one-night stay the storefront chooses (about two weeks out) and that stay is reported under `priced_for` in the response  -  send your own dates for prices you can rely on.

parameters.name: check_out
parameters.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-08`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2026-11-05&check_out=2026-11-08` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Send it together with `check_in`, or omit both.

schema.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-08`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2026-11-05&check_out=2026-11-08` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Send it together with `check_in`, or omit both.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

schema.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

parameters.name: rooms
parameters.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

schema.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

parameters.name: children_ages
parameters.description:
**Ages of the children travelling, comma-separated, each 0 - 17** (e.g. `4,9` for two children aged 4 and 9). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children are placed in the rooms in turn, starting with room 1. Children change both price and availability  -  a room that sleeps two adults may not also take two children.

parameters.name: sort

parameters.name: star_rating
parameters.description:
**Keep only hotels of these star classes, 1 - 5, comma-separated** (e.g. `4` or `4,5`). Optional; every class when omitted.

- Each class includes its half step: `3` keeps 3-star and 3.5-star hotels, `4` keeps 4 and 4.5, and so on.
- Several classes are combined with OR  -  `4,5` keeps 4, 4.5 and 5-star hotels ("4 stars or better").
- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.
- Each returned hotel's class is in its `star_rating`; `applied.star_rating` echoes one class as a number and several as a list.

region_id.description:
**Where to search, as a `region_id` from `/locations`**  -  a city, neighbourhood, landmark, airport or wider region (e.g. `178293` for New York and vicinity, `2734` for Paris). Send this or `destination`.

The most reliable way to name a destination: the id means the same place on every market. An id that matches no destination returns a 404.

destination.description:
**Where to search, as free text** (e.g. `Paris, France`, `Lake Tahoe`, `Las Vegas`). Used only when `region_id` is not sent.

The text is matched to the closest known destination and the matched place is echoed as `destination.resolved_region_id` and `destination.resolved_name`  -  check them, because the matching is loose and a vague or misspelt name can match somewhere unexpected (`blorfington` → "Mall of America, Bloomington, Minnesota"). Text that matches nothing returns a 404. For precise control use `/locations` and pass `region_id`.

check_in.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-05`). Send it together with `check_out`; the two are validated as a pair.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. When both dates are omitted, prices are quoted for a one-night stay the storefront chooses (about two weeks out) and that stay is reported under `priced_for` in the response  -  send your own dates for prices you can rely on.

check_out.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-08`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2026-11-05&check_out=2026-11-08` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Send it together with `check_in`, or omit both.

adults.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

rooms.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

children_ages.description:
**Ages of the children travelling, comma-separated, each 0 - 17** (e.g. `4,9` for two children aged 4 and 9). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children are placed in the rooms in turn, starting with room 1. Children change both price and availability  -  a room that sleeps two adults may not also take two children.

star_rating.description:

- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.

pay_later.description:

The pay-later rate is offered on at least one room of each hotel returned; the headline price on the card may still be a pay-now rate. `false` or omitted applies no payment filter.

available_only.description:
**Drop hotels that have no availability for your dates.** Optional; send `true` to apply.

parameters.name: radius_km
parameters.description:
**Only return hotels within this many kilometres of the point** (0.2 - 50, e.g. `1.5`). Optional; without it the search covers the whole area the point lies in.

- Every hotel returned lies within the radius (`distance_km` at or below it).
- The response echoes `destination.radius_km` and `destination.search_box` (the square around the circle that was searched).
- `dropped_outside_radius` counts the hotels on this page left out because they sit in the corners of that square, so a page can hold fewer than `page_size` hotels while `has_more` is still true.
- `result_count` counts the square, not the circle.
- When the square holds no hotels at all (open sea, polar ice), the response has `returned: 0`, `has_more: false` and `result_count: null`.
- Like any search without filters, the square lists at most about 500 hotels (`coverage`), picked by the storefront's own ranking and not nearest first  -  for a large area, search several smaller circles (or `/hotels/search-by-bounds` tiles) to reach the rest.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

parameters.name: sort

parameters.name: star_rating
parameters.description:
**Keep only hotels of these star classes, 1 - 5, comma-separated** (e.g. `4` or `4,5`). Optional; every class when omitted.

- Each class includes its half step: `3` keeps 3-star and 3.5-star hotels, `4` keeps 4 and 4.5, and so on.
- Several classes are combined with OR  -  `4,5` keeps 4, 4.5 and 5-star hotels ("4 stars or better").
- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.
- Each returned hotel's class is in its `star_rating`; `applied.star_rating` echoes one class as a number and several as a list.

A search without filters stops after roughly 500 hotels whatever the page size (at most about 10 pages of the default 50); a filtered search stops at the end of its selection, whose size is `coverage.max_reachable_results` (up to about 800 with `free_cancellation`).

latitude.description:
**Latitude of the point to search around, in decimal degrees (-90 to 90)**  -  e.g. `40.758` for Times Square. Required, together with `longitude`.

Without `radius_km` the search covers the area the point lies in (its city is echoed as `destination.resolved_region_id` and `resolved_name`); with it, the circle around the point (both are then `null`). Every hotel carries `distance_km` from the point.

longitude.description:
**Longitude of the point to search around, in decimal degrees (-180 to 180)**  -  e.g. `-73.9855` for Times Square. Required, together with `latitude`.

Use the `coordinates` of any `/locations` suggestion or hotel card, or a point from your own map.

radius_km.description:
**Only return hotels within this many kilometres of the point** (0.2 - 50, e.g. `1.5`). Optional; without it the search covers the whole area the point lies in.

- Every hotel returned lies within the radius (`distance_km` at or below it).
- The response echoes `destination.radius_km` and `destination.search_box` (the square around the circle that was searched).
- `dropped_outside_radius` counts the hotels on this page left out because they sit in the corners of that square, so a page can hold fewer than `page_size` hotels while `has_more` is still true.
- `result_count` counts the square, not the circle.
- When the square holds no hotels at all (open sea, polar ice), the response has `returned: 0`, `has_more: false` and `result_count: null`.
- Like any search without filters, the square lists at most about 500 hotels (`coverage`), picked by the storefront's own ranking and not nearest first  -  for a large area, search several smaller circles (or `/hotels/search-by-bounds` tiles) to reach the rest.

check_in.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-05`). Send it together with `check_out`; the two are validated as a pair.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. When both dates are omitted, prices are quoted for a one-night stay the storefront chooses (about two weeks out) and that stay is reported under `priced_for` in the response  -  send your own dates for prices you can rely on.

check_out.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-08`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2026-11-05&check_out=2026-11-08` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Send it together with `check_in`, or omit both.

adults.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

rooms.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

children_ages.description:
**Ages of the children travelling, comma-separated, each 0 - 17** (e.g. `4,9` for two children aged 4 and 9). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children are placed in the rooms in turn, starting with room 1. Children change both price and availability  -  a room that sleeps two adults may not also take two children.

market.description:
**Which Expedia storefront to read from  -  decides the currency of every price and the language of labels and place names.** Optional; defaults to `us`.

Each storefront prices in its own currency and writes its labels (rating words, price notes, neighbourhood names) in its own language. Hotel names stay as the hotel wrote them. Ids (`region_id`, `hotel_id`) are the same on every storefront, so a search can be repeated on another market unchanged.

Some storefronts also offer a second language: `ca_fr` (French), `hk_en`, `tw_en`, `jp_en`, `th_en`, `id_en` (English) and `hk_cn` (Simplified Chinese) are the `ca`, `hk`, `tw`, `jp`, `th` and `id` storefronts  -  same prices, currency and results  -  with their text in that language.

- `us`  -  United States: prices in USD, text in `en`
- `uk`  -  United Kingdom: prices in GBP, text in `en`

sort.description:
**Order of the results.** Optional; defaults to `recommended`.

- `recommended`  -  the storefront's own recommended order (default)
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest first
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive first
- `guest_rating`  -  highest guest score first
- `star_rating`  -  highest star class first
- `member_prices`  -  hotels offering member-only prices first

Sorting reorders the same selection of hotels  -  it never reaches hotels a search does not return (see `coverage` in the response). To see different hotels, change the destination or the filters.

star_rating.description:
**Keep only hotels of these star classes, 1 - 5, comma-separated** (e.g. `4` or `4,5`). Optional; every class when omitted.

- Each class includes its half step: `3` keeps 3-star and 3.5-star hotels, `4` keeps 4 and 4.5, and so on.
- Several classes are combined with OR  -  `4,5` keeps 4, 4.5 and 5-star hotels ("4 stars or better").
- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.
- Each returned hotel's class is in its `star_rating`; `applied.star_rating` echoes one class as a number and several as a list.

guest_rating_min.description:
**Keep only hotels whose guest score (out of 10) is at least this.** Optional; any score when omitted.

- `9`  -  Wonderful, 9+
- `8`  -  Very good, 8+
- `7`  -  Good, 7+

Every returned hotel's score is in `guest_rating.score`. The storefront filters on its own indexed score, which can differ from the displayed one by a few tenths  -  rarely, a hotel shown just under the floor comes back.

price_min.description:
**Lowest price to keep, in the currency of the chosen `market`** (USD on `us`, EUR on `de`, JPY on `jp`, …). Optional; no lower bound when omitted.

Compared with the nightly room rate before taxes and fees by default; set `price_type=total` to compare with the total for the whole stay instead. Hotels with no availability for your dates carry no price and are not excluded by a price filter  -  add `available_only=true` to drop them.

price_max.description:
**Highest price to keep, in the currency of the chosen `market`.** Optional; no upper bound when omitted.

Same basis as `price_min` (`price_type`). Send `price_min` alone for "at least", `price_max` alone for "at most", both for a window  -  e.g. `price_min=100&price_max=250` on `us` keeps nightly rates between $100 and $250.

price_type.description:
**What `price_min` / `price_max` are compared with.** Optional; defaults to `nightly`.

- `nightly`  -  the rate for one room for one night, before taxes and fees
- `total`  -  the total for the whole stay, all nights and rooms

Has no effect unless `price_min` or `price_max` is sent.

free_cancellation.description:
**Keep only hotels with a fully refundable rate** for your dates. Optional; send `true` to apply.

Every hotel returned then has `is_refundable: true`. `false` or omitted applies no cancellation filter.

pay_later.description:
**Keep only hotels offering a "reserve now, pay later" rate.** Optional; send `true` to apply.

The pay-later rate is offered on at least one room of each hotel returned; the headline price on the card may still be a pay-now rate. `false` or omitted applies no payment filter.

available_only.description:
**Drop hotels that have no availability for your dates.** Optional; send `true` to apply.

Without it, a dated search can include hotels that are sold out for those nights  -  they come back with `is_available: false` and `price: null` so you can still see them.

meal_plans.description:
**Keep only hotels offering these meal plans, comma-separated.** Optional. Several values must ALL be offered (so `breakfast_included,all_inclusive` usually matches nothing).

- `breakfast_included` (Breakfast included)

filters.description:

include_star_rating.description:
**Look up each hotel's star class and street address.** Optional; on by default  -  send `false` to skip it.

Including the star class and address adds roughly one to three seconds per page. With `false`, `star_rating` and `address` come back `null` and the response is faster.

page.description:
**Which page of results to return, 1-based.** Optional; defaults to `1`.

Keep paging while `has_more` is true (`next_page` gives the number to send). A search without filters stops after roughly 500 hotels whatever the page size (at most about 10 pages of the default 50); a filtered search stops at the end of its selection, whose size is `coverage.max_reachable_results` (up to about 800 with `free_cancellation`).

page_size.description:
**Hotels per page, 1 - 200.** Optional; defaults to `50`.

Larger pages mean fewer calls but slower responses (200 hotels per page takes a few seconds). Keep the same `page_size` while paging through one search, or pages will overlap.

description: Search hotels inside a rectangular map area.

parameters.name: ne_lat
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the north-east (top-right) corner of the map area, in decimal degrees** (-90 to 90)  -  e.g. `40.78`. Required.

The four corner values describe one rectangle; `sw_lat` must not be above `ne_lat` (a 400 otherwise), and the two corners must differ in both latitude and longitude. A rectangle may cross the 180° meridian: send its west edge as `sw_lng` and its east edge as `ne_lng` (e.g. `sw_lng=177&ne_lng=-179` around Fiji); whenever `sw_lng` is east of `ne_lng`, the narrower of the two possible rectangles is searched. Every hotel returned lies inside the rectangle.

parameters.name: check_in
parameters.description:

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

parameters.name: star_rating
parameters.description:
**Keep only hotels of these star classes, 1 - 5, comma-separated** (e.g. `4` or `4,5`). Optional; every class when omitted.

- Each class includes its half step: `3` keeps 3-star and 3.5-star hotels, `4` keeps 4 and 4.5, and so on.
- Several classes are combined with OR  -  `4,5` keeps 4, 4.5 and 5-star hotels ("4 stars or better").
- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.
- Each returned hotel's class is in its `star_rating`; `applied.star_rating` echoes one class as a number and several as a list.

ne_lat.description:
**Latitude of the north-east (top-right) corner of the map area, in decimal degrees** (-90 to 90)  -  e.g. `40.78`. Required.

The four corner values describe one rectangle; `sw_lat` must not be above `ne_lat` (a 400 otherwise), and the two corners must differ in both latitude and longitude. A rectangle may cross the 180° meridian: send its west edge as `sw_lng` and its east edge as `ne_lng` (e.g. `sw_lng=177&ne_lng=-179` around Fiji); whenever `sw_lng` is east of `ne_lng`, the narrower of the two possible rectangles is searched. Every hotel returned lies inside the rectangle.

check_in.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-05`). Send it together with `check_out`; the two are validated as a pair.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. When both dates are omitted, prices are quoted for a one-night stay the storefront chooses (about two weeks out) and that stay is reported under `priced_for` in the response  -  send your own dates for prices you can rely on.

check_out.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-08`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2026-11-05&check_out=2026-11-08` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Send it together with `check_in`, or omit both.

adults.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

rooms.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

children_ages.description:
**Ages of the children travelling, comma-separated, each 0 - 17** (e.g. `4,9` for two children aged 4 and 9). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children are placed in the rooms in turn, starting with room 1. Children change both price and availability  -  a room that sleeps two adults may not also take two children.

market.description:

sort.description:
**Order of the results.** Optional; defaults to `recommended`.

- `recommended`  -  the storefront's own recommended order (default)
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest first
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive first
- `guest_rating`  -  highest guest score first
- `star_rating`  -  highest star class first
- `member_prices`  -  hotels offering member-only prices first

Sorting reorders the same selection of hotels  -  it never reaches hotels a search does not return (see `coverage` in the response). To see different hotels, change the destination or the filters.

star_rating.description:
**Keep only hotels of these star classes, 1 - 5, comma-separated** (e.g. `4` or `4,5`). Optional; every class when omitted.

- Each class includes its half step: `3` keeps 3-star and 3.5-star hotels, `4` keeps 4 and 4.5, and so on.
- Several classes are combined with OR  -  `4,5` keeps 4, 4.5 and 5-star hotels ("4 stars or better").
- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.
- Each returned hotel's class is in its `star_rating`; `applied.star_rating` echoes one class as a number and several as a list.

guest_rating_min.description:
**Keep only hotels whose guest score (out of 10) is at least this.** Optional; any score when omitted.

- `9`  -  Wonderful, 9+
- `8`  -  Very good, 8+
- `7`  -  Good, 7+

Every returned hotel's score is in `guest_rating.score`. The storefront filters on its own indexed score, which can differ from the displayed one by a few tenths  -  rarely, a hotel shown just under the floor comes back.

price_min.description:
**Lowest price to keep, in the currency of the chosen `market`** (USD on `us`, EUR on `de`, JPY on `jp`, …). Optional; no lower bound when omitted.

Compared with the nightly room rate before taxes and fees by default; set `price_type=total` to compare with the total for the whole stay instead. Hotels with no availability for your dates carry no price and are not excluded by a price filter  -  add `available_only=true` to drop them.

price_max.description:
**Highest price to keep, in the currency of the chosen `market`.** Optional; no upper bound when omitted.

Same basis as `price_min` (`price_type`). Send `price_min` alone for "at least", `price_max` alone for "at most", both for a window  -  e.g. `price_min=100&price_max=250` on `us` keeps nightly rates between $100 and $250.

price_type.description:
**What `price_min` / `price_max` are compared with.** Optional; defaults to `nightly`.

- `nightly`  -  the rate for one room for one night, before taxes and fees
- `total`  -  the total for the whole stay, all nights and rooms

Has no effect unless `price_min` or `price_max` is sent.

free_cancellation.description:
**Keep only hotels with a fully refundable rate** for your dates. Optional; send `true` to apply.

Every hotel returned then has `is_refundable: true`. `false` or omitted applies no cancellation filter.

pay_later.description:
**Keep only hotels offering a "reserve now, pay later" rate.** Optional; send `true` to apply.

The pay-later rate is offered on at least one room of each hotel returned; the headline price on the card may still be a pay-now rate. `false` or omitted applies no payment filter.

available_only.description:
**Drop hotels that have no availability for your dates.** Optional; send `true` to apply.

Without it, a dated search can include hotels that are sold out for those nights  -  they come back with `is_available: false` and `price: null` so you can still see them.

description: Search hotels near an airport by IATA code.

parameters.name: airport_code

An unknown code returns a 404; a city code (e.g. `NYC`, `LON`, `PAR`, `STO`) returns a 400 naming its airports. To browse airports by name, use `/locations?type=flights`.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**Order of the results.** Optional; defaults to `recommended`.

- `recommended`  -  the storefront's own recommended order (default)
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest first
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive first
- `guest_rating`  -  highest guest score first
- `star_rating`  -  highest star class first
- `member_prices`  -  hotels offering member-only prices first

Sorting reorders the same selection of hotels  -  it never reaches hotels a search does not return (see `coverage` in the response). To see different hotels, change the destination or the filters.

parameters.name: star_rating
parameters.description:
**Keep only hotels of these star classes, 1 - 5, comma-separated** (e.g. `4` or `4,5`). Optional; every class when omitted.

- Each class includes its half step: `3` keeps 3-star and 3.5-star hotels, `4` keeps 4 and 4.5, and so on.
- Several classes are combined with OR  -  `4,5` keeps 4, 4.5 and 5-star hotels ("4 stars or better").
- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.
- Each returned hotel's class is in its `star_rating`; `applied.star_rating` echoes one class as a number and several as a list.

Every returned hotel's score is in `guest_rating.score`. The storefront filters on its own indexed score, which can differ from the displayed one by a few tenths  -  rarely, a hotel shown just under the floor comes back.

airport_code.description:
**Three-letter IATA code of the airport** (e.g. `JFK`, `LHR`, `CDG`, `BOM`). Required; case does not matter.

The code is matched to the airport itself (not to a similarly named town) and the airport is echoed under `destination` (`airport_name`, `airport_coordinates`). An unknown code returns a 404; a city code (e.g. `NYC`, `LON`, `PAR`, `STO`) returns a 400 naming its airports. To browse airports by name, use `/locations?type=flights`.

check_in.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-05`). Send it together with `check_out`; the two are validated as a pair.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. When both dates are omitted, prices are quoted for a one-night stay the storefront chooses (about two weeks out) and that stay is reported under `priced_for` in the response  -  send your own dates for prices you can rely on.

check_out.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-11-08`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2026-11-05&check_out=2026-11-08` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Send it together with `check_in`, or omit both.

adults.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

rooms.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

children_ages.description:
**Ages of the children travelling, comma-separated, each 0 - 17** (e.g. `4,9` for two children aged 4 and 9). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children are placed in the rooms in turn, starting with room 1. Children change both price and availability  -  a room that sleeps two adults may not also take two children.

market.description:
**Which Expedia storefront to read from  -  decides the currency of every price and the language of labels and place names.** Optional; defaults to `us`.

Each storefront prices in its own currency and writes its labels (rating words, price notes, neighbourhood names) in its own language. Hotel names stay as the hotel wrote them. Ids (`region_id`, `hotel_id`) are the same on every storefront, so a search can be repeated on another market unchanged.

Some storefronts also offer a second language: `ca_fr` (French), `hk_en`, `tw_en`, `jp_en`, `th_en`, `id_en` (English) and `hk_cn` (Simplified Chinese) are the `ca`, `hk`, `tw`, `jp`, `th` and `id` storefronts  -  same prices, currency and results  -  with their text in that language.

**Order of the results.** Optional; defaults to `recommended`.

- `recommended`  -  the storefront's own recommended order (default)
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest first
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive first
- `guest_rating`  -  highest guest score first
- `star_rating`  -  highest star class first
- `member_prices`  -  hotels offering member-only prices first

Sorting reorders the same selection of hotels  -  it never reaches hotels a search does not return (see `coverage` in the response). To see different hotels, change the destination or the filters.

star_rating.description:
**Keep only hotels of these star classes, 1 - 5, comma-separated** (e.g. `4` or `4,5`). Optional; every class when omitted.

- Each class includes its half step: `3` keeps 3-star and 3.5-star hotels, `4` keeps 4 and 4.5, and so on.
- Several classes are combined with OR  -  `4,5` keeps 4, 4.5 and 5-star hotels ("4 stars or better").
- Every available hotel of each class is listed, but a combined list can leave out some sold-out hotels  -  search one class at a time if you need those too.
- Each returned hotel's class is in its `star_rating`; `applied.star_rating` echoes one class as a number and several as a list.

guest_rating_min.description:
**Keep only hotels whose guest score (out of 10) is at least this.** Optional; any score when omitted.

- `9`  -  Wonderful, 9+
- `8`  -  Very good, 8+
- `7`  -  Good, 7+

Every returned hotel's score is in `guest_rating.score`. The storefront filters on its own indexed score, which can differ from the displayed one by a few tenths  -  rarely, a hotel shown just under the floor comes back.

price_min.description:
**Lowest price to keep, in the currency of the chosen `market`** (USD on `us`, EUR on `de`, JPY on `jp`, …). Optional; no lower bound when omitted.

Compared with the nightly room rate before taxes and fees by default; set `price_type=total` to compare with the total for the whole stay instead. Hotels with no availability for your dates carry no price and are not excluded by a price filter  -  add `available_only=true` to drop them.

price_max.description:
**Highest price to keep, in the currency of the chosen `market`.** Optional; no upper bound when omitted.

Same basis as `price_min` (`price_type`). Send `price_min` alone for "at least", `price_max` alone for "at most", both for a window  -  e.g. `price_min=100&price_max=250` on `us` keeps nightly rates between $100 and $250.

price_type.description:
**What `price_min` / `price_max` are compared with.** Optional; defaults to `nightly`.

- `nightly`  -  the rate for one room for one night, before taxes and fees
- `total`  -  the total for the whole stay, all nights and rooms

Has no effect unless `price_min` or `price_max` is sent.

free_cancellation.description:
**Keep only hotels with a fully refundable rate** for your dates. Optional; send `true` to apply.

Every hotel returned then has `is_refundable: true`. `false` or omitted applies no cancellation filter.

pay_later.description:
**Keep only hotels offering a "reserve now, pay later" rate.** Optional; send `true` to apply.

The pay-later rate is offered on at least one room of each hotel returned; the headline price on the card may still be a pay-now rate. `false` or omitted applies no payment filter.

available_only.description:
**Drop hotels that have no availability for your dates.** Optional; send `true` to apply.

Without it, a dated search can include hotels that are sold out for those nights  -  they come back with `is_available: false` and `price: null` so you can still see them.

room_amenities.description:
**Keep only properties whose rooms have ALL of these amenities, comma-separated** (e.g. `kitchen` or `safe,blackout_curtains`). Optional.

- `porch_lanai` (Porch or lanai)
- `private_bathroom` (Private bathroom)
- `blackout_curtains` (Blackout curtains)
- `air_conditioning` (Air conditioning)
- `accessibility_features` (Accessibility features)
- `top_floor` (Top floor)
- `private_hot_tub` (Private hot tub)
- `jetted_tub` (Jetted or soaking bathtub)
- `in_room_entertainment` (In-room entertainment)
- `safe` (Personal safe)
- `yard` (Yard)
- `fireplace` (Fireplace)
- `wifi` (WiFi)
- `refrigerator` (Refrigerator)
- `coffee_tea_maker` (Coffee/tea maker)
- `private_sauna` (Private sauna)
- `swim_up_room` (Swim-up room)
- `kitchen` (Kitchen or kitchenette)
- `private_pool` (Private pool)
- `ground_floor` (Ground floor)

- `iron_and_board` (Iron and board)
- `microwave` (Microwave)
- `oven` (Oven)
- `dishwasher` (Dishwasher)

These are in-room features; property-wide amenities (pool, parking, gym, …) are `amenities`.

member_benefits.description:
**Keep only properties with ALL of these One Key member benefits, comma-separated** (e.g. `vip_access`). Optional.

- `vip_access` (VIP Access properties)
- `member_prices` (Member Prices)
- `discounted` (Discounted properties)

The matching benefit shows on each card as a `badges` entry (e.g. "VIP Access", "Member Price $201 off") or a `strikethrough` price. To rank member deals first without filtering, use `sort=member_prices`.

brand_ids.description:
**Keep only hotels of these brands**, as comma-separated numeric brand ids (e.g. `28` for Courtyard by Marriott). Optional. Several brands are combined with OR.

Brand ids come from the `Property brand` group of `/hotels/search-filters` for your destination; the list of brands differs per destination and changes over time.

hotel_name.description:
**Keep only hotels whose name contains this text** (e.g. `Hilton`, `Pod`). Optional.

Matching is loose (partial words and close spellings match). Plain text only  -  angle brackets, braces and similar markup characters are rejected with a 400.

filters.description:
**Any other filter, as comma-separated `group:value` tokens copied from `/hotels/search-filters`** (each option's `filter_token`). Optional.

The bed-count tokens (`king_bed_gt:2`, …) are a storefront experiment applied on only some searches (see `/hotels/search-filters`).

exclude_hotel_ids.description:

include_star_rating.description:

Including the star class and address adds roughly one to three seconds per page. With `false`, `star_rating` and `address` come back `null` and the response is faster.

page.description:
**Which page of results to return, 1-based.** Optional; defaults to `1`.

Keep paging while `has_more` is true (`next_page` gives the number to send). A search without filters stops after roughly 500 hotels whatever the page size (at most about 10 pages of the default 50); a filtered search stops at the end of its selection, whose size is `coverage.max_reachable_results` (up to about 800 with `free_cancellation`).

page_size.description:
**Hotels per page, 1 - 200.** Optional; defaults to `50`.

Larger pages mean fewer calls but slower responses (200 hotels per page takes a few seconds). Keep the same `page_size` while paging through one search, or pages will overlap.

parameters.name: check_in
parameters.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2027-06-15`). Required, together with `check_out`.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. Room availability and every price in the response are for exactly this stay.

parameters.name: check_out
parameters.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2027-06-18`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2027-06-15&check_out=2027-06-18` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Properties sold room by room (hotels, aparthotels, and rentals listed like hotels) are sold for at most 28 nights per booking: a longer stay there is rejected with a 400 that names the limit. Whole-home vacation rentals set their own longest stay (one that cannot take the stay answers `is_available: false`). Any other stay the property cannot host returns `is_available: false` with the reason in `unavailable_message`, not an error.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

hotel_id.description:
**The hotel to look up, as its `hotel_id`**  -  the id on every hotel card returned by `/hotels/search`, `/hotels/search-by-coordinates`, `/hotels/batch`, and on hotel results from `/locations` (e.g. `17117062`). Required.

Hotels and vacation rentals share one id space, and an id means the same property on every `market`. An id that does not exist returns a 404 with a hint.

check_in.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2027-06-15`). Required, together with `check_out`.

Must be today or later, and the stay must end within 500 days of today. Room availability and every price in the response are for exactly this stay.

check_out.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2027-06-18`)  -  the morning you leave, so `check_in=2027-06-15&check_out=2027-06-18` is three nights.

Must be at least one day after `check_in` and no more than 500 days from today. Properties sold room by room (hotels, aparthotels, and rentals listed like hotels) are sold for at most 28 nights per booking: a longer stay there is rejected with a 400 that names the limit. Whole-home vacation rentals set their own longest stay (one that cannot take the stay answers `is_available: false`). Any other stay the property cannot host returns `is_available: false` with the reason in `unavailable_message`, not an error.

adults.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

rooms.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

**Ages of the children travelling, comma-separated, each 0 - 17** (e.g. `4,9` for two children aged 4 and 9). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children are placed in the rooms in turn, starting with room 1. Children change both price and availability  -  a room that sleeps two adults may not also take two children.

parameters.name: check_in
parameters.description:
**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2027-06-15`). Optional  -  send it together with `check_out` to price every similar property for that stay and party.

Without dates the platform still shows a price per property, for a stay it picks itself (usually one night a couple of weeks ahead); each card says which stay in `price_check_in` / `price_check_out`. With dates, the stay must start today or later and end within 500 days.

Without dates the platform still shows a price per property, for a stay it picks itself (usually one night a couple of weeks ahead); each card says which stay in `price_check_in` / `price_check_out`. With dates, the stay must start today or later and end within 500 days.

parameters.name: check_out
parameters.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2027-06-18`)  -  the morning you leave. Optional; send it together with `check_in`, or omit both.

Must be at least one day after `check_in`. A lone `check_in` or `check_out` is rejected with a 400 that says to send both.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

parameters.name: rooms
parameters.description:
**Number of rooms to book** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

With more than one room, `price.total` is for all rooms together while `price.per_night` stays the rate for one room for one night. `adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult.

parameters.name: children_ages
parameters.description:
**Ages of the children travelling, comma-separated, each 0 - 17** (e.g. `4,9` for two children aged 4 and 9). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children are placed in the rooms in turn, starting with room 1. Children change both price and availability  -  a room that sleeps two adults may not also take two children.

parameters.name: market

**Which Expedia storefront to read from  -  decides the currency of every price and the language of labels and place names.** Optional; defaults to `us`.

Each storefront prices in its own currency and writes its labels (rating words, price notes, neighbourhood names) in its own language. Hotel names stay as the hotel wrote them. Ids (`region_id`, `hotel_id`) are the same on every storefront, so a search can be repeated on another market unchanged.

description: Read a hotel's guest reviews with replies, photos and themes  -  sortable and keyword-searchable.

parameters.name: hotel_id
parameters.description:
**The hotel to read, as its numeric `hotel_id`** (e.g. `17117062`). Required.

Take it from any hotel card returned by `/hotels/search` (and its sibling searches), from a `/locations` hotel result, or from the `.h.` part of a hotel page URL (`…/New-York-Hotels-PUBLIC.h17117062.Hotel-Information` → `17117062`). The id is the same on every market. An id that names no hotel returns a 404.

schema.description:
**The hotel to read, as its numeric `hotel_id`** (e.g. `17117062`). Required.

Take it from any hotel card returned by `/hotels/search` (and its sibling searches), from a `/locations` hotel result, or from the `.h.` part of a hotel page URL (`…/New-York-Hotels-PUBLIC.h17117062.Hotel-Information` → `17117062`). The id is the same on every market. An id that names no hotel returns a 404.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**Order of the reviews.** Optional; defaults to `most_relevant`.

- `most_relevant`  -  the storefront's own "Most relevant" order (default): recent reviews, with reviews written in the market's language first. On English-language markets the first 4 pages are the storefront's pick of 200 reviews and later pages continue newest first (a picked review is not repeated), so a few recent reviews the pick skipped only appear under `most_recent`
- `most_recent`  -  newest first, by submission date  -  the order to use to page through every review
- `highest_rated`  -  highest guest rating first (newest first within a rating)
- `lowest_rated`  -  lowest guest rating first (newest first within a rating)  -  the fastest way to read complaints

Cannot be combined with `search` (keyword matches always come newest first); sending both returns a 400.

Cannot be combined with `search` (keyword matches always come newest first); sending both returns a 400.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description:
**Only reviews that mention this word or phrase** (e.g. `breakfast`, `pool`, `parking`). Optional.

Only reviews written in the `market`'s language are searched  -  on `de` a German word such as `Zimmer` finds German reviews while `breakfast` finds none  -  so search English words on an English-language market such as `us`. The response then carries `matching_reviews` (the platform's approximate count, at most 400  -  only about half of it can be paged through) next to the hotel's `total_reviews`, and the matches come newest first. Matching is loose  -  close spellings match too (`pool` also finds "poor")  -  and the searchable archive can lag a few months behind the newest reviews, so very recent reviews may not be found yet. Plain text only: angle brackets, braces, back-ticks, `..`, `--` and similar markup are rejected with a 400. Keyword matches carry `language: null` (the platform labels every match with the market's locale rather than the review's own).

parameters.description:

About 95-98% of a hotel's reviews can be paged through (the oldest are counted in `total_reviews` but not served  -  on busy hotels nothing older than about three years), so the final page arrives before `total_reviews` is reached. A page past the end returns no reviews.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

parameters.name: rooms
parameters.description:
**Number of rooms** (1 - 8). Optional; defaults to `1`.

`adults` must be at least `rooms`, because every room needs an adult. With several rooms `price` covers all of them together, and a multi-room stay can come back without a verdict (`no_comparison_data`) where the one-room stay has one.

**First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-12-09`). Optional  -  send it together with `check_out`, or omit both for a 3-night stay starting 14 days from today (echoed as `check_in` / `check_out` with `dates_chosen_automatically: true`).

Must be today or later. Verdicts are published for stays up to about three months ahead; for a later stay `insight_available` is usually `false` with `unavailable_reason: no_comparison_data`.

check_out.description:
**Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (e.g. `2026-12-12`). Optional; send it together with `check_in`.

adults.description:
**Total number of adults in the party**, across all rooms. Optional; defaults to `2`.

Adults are spread as evenly as possible over `rooms` (earlier rooms take the extra one), and every room needs at least one adult  -  so `rooms=2&adults=5` books rooms of 3 and 2. At most 14 adults per room. Prices change with the party size, and some hotels have no room for a large party on a given night.

rooms.description:

children_ages.description:

return_date.description:

adults.description:
**Number of adult travellers (age 18+).** Optional; defaults to `1`.

At most 9 travellers in total across `adults`, `children_ages`, `infants_in_lap` and `infants_in_seat`. `price.total` covers everyone; `price.per_traveler` is that total divided by the travellers who have a seat (lap infants excluded, as on the storefront), exact to the cent (the storefront's rounded headline figure is `price.per_traveler_formatted`).

children_ages.description:
**Ages of child travellers (2 - 17), comma-separated** (e.g. `5,11` for two children). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children under 2 travel as infants  -  use `infants_in_lap` or `infants_in_seat` instead. Child fares are included in `price.total`.

infants_in_lap.description:
**Number of infants (under 2) travelling on an adult's lap.** Optional; defaults to `0`.

Each lap infant needs an adult, so this cannot exceed `adults`. Lap infants usually travel free or for a small fee; any fee is in `price.total`, and they are not counted in `price.per_traveler` (they have no seat).

infants_in_seat.description:
**Number of infants (under 2) with their own seat.** Optional; defaults to `0`.

An infant in a seat is priced like a traveller and counts towards the 9-traveller limit.

cabin_class.description:
**Cabin to search.** Optional; defaults to `economy`.

- `economy`  -  Economy (default)
- `premium_economy`  -  Premium economy
- `business`  -  Business
- `first`  -  First

One cabin per search  -  to compare cabins, run one search per cabin. On routes where the requested cabin does not exist (e.g. business on many domestic US flights) the next cabin up is offered instead; each segment's `cabin_label` shows what is actually sold.

include_nearby_airports.description:
**Also search airports near `origin` and `destination`.** Optional; send `true` to widen.

By default an airport code means exactly that airport. With `true`, the storefront adds the nearby airports it groups with it  -  e.g. `SEA` also finds flights from Seattle Paine Field (PAE); many airports have no such group and are unchanged. The airports actually served are listed in `summary.departure_airports` / `summary.arrival_airports`. For every airport of a city use its metro code (`NYC`, `LON`).

parameters.name: outbound_token
parameters.description:
**The `outbound_token` of the outbound itinerary you chose**, copied from a `/flights/search` call that had a `return_date`. Required.

Send the SAME `origin`, `destination`, `departure_date`, `return_date`, travellers and `cabin_class` as that search. Tokens belong to one search session and stop working after a while  -  if a token is refused (404), run `/flights/search` again and use a fresh one.

What a token cannot check: another `origin` / `destination` / `departure_date` is refused (404) or finds no flights, but another `return_date` or party is quietly priced for what you send, and the CABIN always follows the token  -  an economy token sent with `cabin_class=business` lists economy fares while `trip.cabin_class` echoes `business`. The token does not reliably name its cabin (a first-class search was seen labelled Business), so this cannot be refused here: keep `cabin_class` unchanged.

outbound_token.description:
**The `outbound_token` of the outbound itinerary you chose**, copied from a `/flights/search` call that had a `return_date`. Required.

Send the SAME `origin`, `destination`, `departure_date`, `return_date`, travellers and `cabin_class` as that search. Tokens belong to one search session and stop working after a while  -  if a token is refused (404), run `/flights/search` again and use a fresh one.

What a token cannot check: another `origin` / `destination` / `departure_date` is refused (404) or finds no flights, but another `return_date` or party is quietly priced for what you send, and the CABIN always follows the token  -  an economy token sent with `cabin_class=business` lists economy fares while `trip.cabin_class` echoes `business`. The token does not reliably name its cabin (a first-class search was seen labelled Business), so this cannot be refused here: keep `cabin_class` unchanged.

An airport code searches that airport only (see `include_nearby_airports`); a metro code searches all of its airports. Codes are checked before searching: an unknown code returns a 404. Find codes with `/locations?type=flights` (`airport_code`, or `hierarchy.metro_code` for the metro area).

An infant in a seat is priced like a traveller and counts towards the 9-traveller limit.

cabin_class.description:
**Cabin to search.** Optional; defaults to `economy`.

- `economy`  -  Economy (default)
- `premium_economy`  -  Premium economy
- `business`  -  Business
- `first`  -  First

One cabin per search  -  to compare cabins, run one search per cabin. On routes where the requested cabin does not exist (e.g. business on many domestic US flights) the next cabin up is offered instead; each segment's `cabin_label` shows what is actually sold.

include_nearby_airports.description:
**Also search airports near `origin` and `destination`.** Optional; send `true` to widen.

By default an airport code means exactly that airport. With `true`, the storefront adds the nearby airports it groups with it  -  e.g. `SEA` also finds flights from Seattle Paine Field (PAE); many airports have no such group and are unchanged. The airports actually served are listed in `summary.departure_airports` / `summary.arrival_airports`. For every airport of a city use its metro code (`NYC`, `LON`).

- `arrival_latest`  -  latest arrival first

stops.description:
**Keep only itineraries with this many stops.** Optional; any number when omitted.

- `nonstop`  -  direct flights only
- `one_stop`  -  exactly one connection
- `two_or_more`  -  two or more connections

Every returned itinerary's `journeys[].stops` matches. `summary.stops` shows how many itineraries exist per stop count and the cheapest price of each, so you can see beforehand whether a nonstop exists.

airlines.description:
**Keep only itineraries flown by these airlines, as comma-separated two-character IATA codes** (e.g. `DL`, `BA,AA`). Optional. Several codes are combined with OR.

An itinerary matches when any of its flights is sold by a listed airline (so `DL` also returns a United + Delta connection). The airlines serving the route, with codes, itinerary counts and cheapest prices, are in `summary.airlines` of any search on it.

departure_times.description:
**Keep only itineraries departing in these parts of the day, comma-separated** (local time at the departure airport). Optional. Several values are combined with OR.

- `early_morning`  -  12:00am - 4:59am
- `morning`  -  5:00am - 11:59am
- `afternoon`  -  12:00pm - 5:59pm
- `evening`  -  6:00pm - 11:59pm

arrival_times.description:
**Keep only itineraries arriving in these parts of the day, comma-separated** (local time at the arrival airport). Optional. Several values are combined with OR.

- `early_morning`  -  12:00am - 4:59am
- `morning`  -  5:00am - 11:59am
- `afternoon`  -  12:00pm - 5:59pm
- `evening`  -  6:00pm - 11:59pm

refundable_only.description:
**Keep only itineraries with a refundable fare**, and price each at its cheapest refundable fare. Optional; send `true` to apply.

The headline price then belongs to that refundable fare (usually higher than the basic fare): one with NO cancellation fee  -  `fare_options[0].refundable` is `included` on every result on English-language storefronts (a fare refundable for a fee, `fee`, does not qualify).

seat_choice_included.description:
**Keep only fares that include choosing a seat**, pricing each itinerary at its cheapest such fare. Optional; send `true` to apply.

Useful to skip basic-economy fares that do not allow seat selection. `fare_options[0].seat_choice` is `included` on the results.

changes_included.description:
**Keep only fares that allow changes without a change fee** (you pay only any fare difference), pricing each itinerary at its cheapest such fare. Optional; send `true` to apply.

`fare_options[0].changes` is `included` on the results.

carry_on_included.description:
**Keep only fares that include a carry-on bag**, pricing each itinerary at its cheapest such fare. Optional; send `true` to apply.

Mostly matters on low-cost and European carriers, whose cheapest fares charge for cabin bags.

max_price.description:
**Highest price per traveller to keep, in the currency of the chosen `market`** (USD on `us`, GBP on `uk`, EUR on `de`). Optional.

Compared with `price.per_traveler` (the one-way or round-trip price per seated traveller, taxes included). Every returned itinerary is at or below it; `total_itineraries` counts only those.

departure_airports.description:
**Keep only itineraries leaving from these airports, as comma-separated three-letter IATA codes** (e.g. `EWR`, `EWR,JFK`). Optional. Several codes are combined with OR.

Picks airports within a metro-code search (`origin=NYC`) or a nearby-airports search (`include_nearby_airports=true`); the airports on offer, with itinerary counts and cheapest prices, are in `summary.departure_airports`. Every returned itinerary's first `origin.code` is one of them.

arrival_airports.description:
**Keep only itineraries arriving at these airports, as comma-separated three-letter IATA codes** (e.g. `LGW`, `LHR,LCY`). Optional. Several codes are combined with OR.

The airports on offer are in `summary.arrival_airports`. Every returned itinerary's final `destination.code` is one of them.

max_layover_hours.description:
**Longest single connection to keep, in hours** (e.g. `1.5` for 90 minutes). Optional.

Every layover of every returned itinerary (`journeys[].layovers[].duration_minutes`) is at or under it; nonstop itineraries are kept.

amenities.description:
**Keep only itineraries with ALL of these on-board amenities, comma-separated.** Optional.

- `wifi`  -  Wi-Fi on board
- `power`  -  in-seat power
- `entertainment`  -  on-demand entertainment

Every returned itinerary's `journeys[].amenities` lists them (as `wifi`, `power`, `ondemand_entertainment`).

page.description:
**Which page of itineraries to return, 1-based.** Optional; defaults to `1`.

Keep paging while `has_more` is true (`next_page` gives the number to send); the pages together cover every itinerary counted in `total_itineraries`. Later pages answer in about the same time as the first.

page_size.description:
**Itineraries per page, 1 - 100.** Optional; defaults to `25`.

Keep the same `page_size` while paging through one search, or pages will overlap. Each itinerary carries every segment and fare family, so a page of 100 is roughly 0.5 - 0.7 MB.

max_duration_hours.description:
**Longest total travel time to keep, in hours, door-to-door from first departure to last arrival** (e.g. `9` or `12.5`). Optional.

Compared with `journeys[].duration_minutes` (layovers included). Every returned itinerary is at or under it.

description: Search a multi-city trip of 2 - 5 flights, one flight at a time, each option priced as the whole trip.

parameters.name: legs
parameters.description:
**The flights of the trip, in order, comma-separated, each as `ORIGIN-DESTINATION-YYYY-MM-DD`** (2 - 5 flights; e.g. `JFK-LHR-2027-06-15,LHR-CDG-2027-06-19,CDG-JFK-2027-06-24`). Required.

Codes are three-letter IATA airport or metro codes (`NYC`, `LON`), resolved like `origin` on `/flights/search`; an unknown code returns a 404. Dates must be in order, today or later and within 330 days of today. An open jaw (`JFK-LHR-…,CDG-JFK-…`) is allowed.

parameters.name: next_token
parameters.description:
**Continue the trip: the `next_token` of the itinerary you chose on the previous flight.** Optional; omit it to list flight 1.

Each step lists the options for ONE flight of `legs`: without a token flight 1, with the `next_token` of a flight-1 itinerary flight 2, and so on (`trip.step`). Send the SAME `legs`, travellers and `cabin_class` on every step. Tokens belong to one search session and stop working after a while  -  a refused token returns a 404; start again from flight 1.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description:
**Number of adult travellers (age 18+).** Optional; defaults to `1`.

At most 9 travellers in total across `adults`, `children_ages`, `infants_in_lap` and `infants_in_seat`. `price.total` covers everyone; `price.per_traveler` is that total divided by the travellers who have a seat (lap infants excluded, as on the storefront), exact to the cent (the storefront's rounded headline figure is `price.per_traveler_formatted`).

legs.description:
**The flights of the trip, in order, comma-separated, each as `ORIGIN-DESTINATION-YYYY-MM-DD`** (2 - 5 flights; e.g. `JFK-LHR-2027-06-15,LHR-CDG-2027-06-19,CDG-JFK-2027-06-24`). Required.

Codes are three-letter IATA airport or metro codes (`NYC`, `LON`), resolved like `origin` on `/flights/search`; an unknown code returns a 404. Dates must be in order, today or later and within 330 days of today. An open jaw (`JFK-LHR-…,CDG-JFK-…`) is allowed.

next_token.description:
**Continue the trip: the `next_token` of the itinerary you chose on the previous flight.** Optional; omit it to list flight 1.

Each step lists the options for ONE flight of `legs`: without a token flight 1, with the `next_token` of a flight-1 itinerary flight 2, and so on (`trip.step`). Send the SAME `legs`, travellers and `cabin_class` on every step. Tokens belong to one search session and stop working after a while  -  a refused token returns a 404; start again from flight 1.

adults.description:
**Number of adult travellers (age 18+).** Optional; defaults to `1`.

At most 9 travellers in total across `adults`, `children_ages`, `infants_in_lap` and `infants_in_seat`. `price.total` covers everyone; `price.per_traveler` is that total divided by the travellers who have a seat (lap infants excluded, as on the storefront), exact to the cent (the storefront's rounded headline figure is `price.per_traveler_formatted`).

children_ages.description:
**Ages of child travellers (2 - 17), comma-separated** (e.g. `5,11` for two children). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children under 2 travel as infants  -  use `infants_in_lap` or `infants_in_seat` instead. Child fares are included in `price.total`.

infants_in_lap.description:
**Number of infants (under 2) travelling on an adult's lap.** Optional; defaults to `0`.

Each lap infant needs an adult, so this cannot exceed `adults`. Lap infants usually travel free or for a small fee; any fee is in `price.total`, and they are not counted in `price.per_traveler` (they have no seat).

infants_in_seat.description:
**Number of infants (under 2) with their own seat.** Optional; defaults to `0`.

An infant in a seat is priced like a traveller and counts towards the 9-traveller limit.

cabin_class.description:
**Cabin to search.** Optional; defaults to `economy`.

- `economy`  -  Economy (default)
- `premium_economy`  -  Premium economy
- `business`  -  Business
- `first`  -  First

One cabin per search  -  to compare cabins, run one search per cabin. On routes where the requested cabin does not exist (e.g. business on many domestic US flights) the next cabin up is offered instead; each segment's `cabin_label` shows what is actually sold.

include_nearby_airports.description:
**Also search airports near `origin` and `destination`.** Optional; send `true` to widen.

By default an airport code means exactly that airport. With `true`, the storefront adds the nearby airports it groups with it  -  e.g. `SEA` also finds flights from Seattle Paine Field (PAE); many airports have no such group and are unchanged. The airports actually served are listed in `summary.departure_airports` / `summary.arrival_airports`. For every airport of a city use its metro code (`NYC`, `LON`).

market.description:
**Which Expedia storefront to read from  -  decides the currency of every price and the language of labels and place names.** Optional; defaults to `us`.

Each storefront prices in its own currency and writes its labels (rating words, price notes, neighbourhood names) in its own language. Hotel names stay as the hotel wrote them. Ids (`region_id`, `hotel_id`) are the same on every storefront, so a search can be repeated on another market unchanged.

Some storefronts also offer a second language: `ca_fr` (French), `hk_en`, `tw_en`, `jp_en`, `th_en`, `id_en` (English) and `hk_cn` (Simplified Chinese) are the `ca`, `hk`, `tw`, `jp`, `th` and `id` storefronts  -  same prices, currency and results  -  with their text in that language.

sort.description:
**Order of the itineraries across every page.** Optional; defaults to `recommended`.

- `recommended`  -  the storefront's own ranking of price, stops and duration (default)
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest first
- `price_high_to_low`  -  most expensive first
- `duration_shortest`  -  shortest total travel time first
- `duration_longest`  -  longest total travel time first
- `departure_earliest`  -  earliest departure first
- `departure_latest`  -  latest departure first
- `arrival_earliest`  -  earliest arrival first
- `arrival_latest`  -  latest arrival first

The whole result set is sorted, then paged with `page` / `page_size`: `price_low_to_high` page 1 is the cheapest itineraries, the last page the most expensive.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description:

An airport code searches that airport only (see `include_nearby_airports`); a metro code searches all of its airports. Codes are checked before searching: an unknown code returns a 404. Find codes with `/locations?type=flights` (`airport_code`, or `hierarchy.metro_code` for the metro area).

**Three-letter IATA code of the departure airport or metro area** (e.g. `JFK`, `LHR`, `SEA`, or `NYC` / `LON` for every airport of the city). Required; case does not matter.

An airport code searches that airport only (see `include_nearby_airports`); a metro code searches all of its airports. Codes are checked before searching: an unknown code returns a 404. Find codes with `/locations?type=flights` (`airport_code`, or `hierarchy.metro_code` for the metro area).

destination.description:

departure_date.description:
**Date of the outbound flight, as `YYYY-MM-DD`** (local date at the departure airport). Required.

Must be today or later and within 330 days of today. Every price in the response is for this date (and `return_date` when sent).

return_date.description:
**Date of the return flight, as `YYYY-MM-DD`**  -  send it for a round trip, omit it for one way. Optional.

Must be on or after `departure_date`. With a return date the results are the OUTBOUND flights priced as round trips ("from" the cheapest matching return); pass an itinerary's `outbound_token` to `/flights/search-return` to list the return flights for it.

adults.description:
**Number of adult travellers (age 18+).** Optional; defaults to `1`.

At most 9 travellers in total across `adults`, `children_ages`, `infants_in_lap` and `infants_in_seat`. `price.total` covers everyone; `price.per_traveler` is that total divided by the travellers who have a seat (lap infants excluded, as on the storefront), exact to the cent (the storefront's rounded headline figure is `price.per_traveler_formatted`).

children_ages.description:
**Ages of child travellers (2 - 17), comma-separated** (e.g. `5,11` for two children). Optional; no children when omitted.

One age per child. Children under 2 travel as infants  -  use `infants_in_lap` or `infants_in_seat` instead. Child fares are included in `price.total`.

infants_in_lap.description:
**Number of infants (under 2) travelling on an adult's lap.** Optional; defaults to `0`.

Each lap infant needs an adult, so this cannot exceed `adults`. Lap infants usually travel free or for a small fee; any fee is in `price.total`, and they are not counted in `price.per_traveler` (they have no seat).

infants_in_seat.description:
**Number of infants (under 2) with their own seat.** Optional; defaults to `0`.

An infant in a seat is priced like a traveller and counts towards the 9-traveller limit.

cabin_class.description:
**Cabin to search.** Optional; defaults to `economy`.

- `economy`  -  Economy (default)
- `premium_economy`  -  Premium economy
- `business`  -  Business
- `first`  -  First

One cabin per search  -  to compare cabins, run one search per cabin. On routes where the requested cabin does not exist (e.g. business on many domestic US flights) the next cabin up is offered instead; each segment's `cabin_label` shows what is actually sold.

include_nearby_airports.description:
**Also search airports near `origin` and `destination`.** Optional; send `true` to widen.

By default an airport code means exactly that airport. With `true`, the storefront adds the nearby airports it groups with it  -  e.g. `SEA` also finds flights from Seattle Paine Field (PAE); many airports have no such group and are unchanged. The airports actually served are listed in `summary.departure_airports` / `summary.arrival_airports`. For every airport of a city use its metro code (`NYC`, `LON`).

description: Search rental cars at an airport or in a city for pick-up and drop-off dates and times.

parameters.name: pickup_location
parameters.description:
**Where to pick the car up: a three-letter airport code** (e.g. `SEA`, `LAX`, `CDG`) **or a numeric `region_id`** from `/locations?type=cars` (a city or neighbourhood, e.g. `6139057` for Detroit).

Airport codes search the rental counters serving that airport (in-terminal and shuttle); a city `region_id` searches branches across the city and makes `sort=distance` meaningful. An unknown airport code or region returns a 404.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**Order of the offers  -  and which 25 you get.** Optional; defaults to `recommended`.

- `recommended`  -  the storefront's own ranking (default)
- `price_low_to_high`  -  cheapest total first
- `distance`  -  nearest supplier branch first (city searches; same as `recommended` at an airport)

A search returns at most 25 offers and the sort decides which: `price_low_to_high` returns the 25 cheapest, which mostly differ from the recommended 25. Run several sorts, or narrow with filters, to see more of `total_cars`.

parameters.description:
**Keep only these car types, comma-separated** (e.g. `suv`, `compact,midsize`). Optional. Several values are combined with OR.

Accepted values: `mini`, `economy`, `compact`, `midsize`, `standard`, `fullsize`, `premium`, `luxury`, `convertible`, `minivan`, `suv`, `van`, `pickup`, `sports_car`, `other`. The types on offer for your search, with their cheapest price, are listed in `available_filters.car_types`.

parameters.name: suppliers

The suppliers differ per location and market  -  read them from a search at the same location on the same `market`: some storefronts list names (`hertz`, `alamo rent a car` on `us`), others two-letter supplier codes (`ZE`, `AL` for LHR on `uk`/`de`/`fr`/`au`; each offer's `supplier.code`). A value the search does not list returns a 400 that lists the ones it does.
